candidates.source_name: MONEYVAL (Council of Europe) — Montenegro country evaluation page
candidates.why_relevant: MONEYVAL is the binding external AML/CFT assessor for Montenegro. Its 5th-round Mutual Evaluation Report (Dec 2023) and enhanced follow-up reports (latest adopted at the 70th plenary, 15-18 Dec 2025, published Jan 2026) carry dated re-reporting obligations (Montenegro to report back within one year) that drive Montenegrin legislative and supervisory deadlines for banks, PSPs and DNFBPs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML crawl of the jurisdiction page + PDF harvest of each evaluation/follow-up report; align polling to MONEYVAL plenary calendar (typically 2-3 plenaries/year).
queries_used: MONEYVAL Montenegro follow-up report AML compliance
MONEYVAL Montenegro fifth round mutual evaluation report

candidates.source_name: FATF Global Network — Montenegro country hub (mirrors MONEYVAL MER/FUR)
candidates.why_relevant: FATF republishes the MONEYVAL Montenegro Mutual Evaluation Report (2023) and Follow-Up Reports (2025) in stable, machine-fetchable PDF form, plus technical-compliance rating tables per FATF Recommendation. Ratings deltas are the single cleanest quantitative signal of Montenegrin AML regulatory change affecting banks and PSPs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Direct PDF fetch of MER/FUR coredownload URLs; parse the technical-compliance rating annex table into a ratings time-series.
queries_used: MONEYVAL Montenegro follow-up report AML compliance

candidates.source_name: IMF — Montenegro country page (Article IV consultations, staff reports, press releases)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual Article IV consultation is the most reliable dated external assessment of Montenegro's banking sector. The 2025 Article IV (Board concluded 18 Nov 2025, PR 25/381) addressed rapid private-sector credit growth, cash loans, real-estate exposure, supervision quality, AML enforcement and SEPA integration — all directly bearing on bank regulation and supervisory tightening.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the IMF country page and Country Report (CR) series quarterly; fetch the staff-report PDF and extract the Financial Sector / FSAP-follow-up sections and the policy-commitment table.
queries_used: IMF Montenegro Article IV financial sector assessment banking
IMF World Bank Montenegro financial sector assessment recommendations

candidates.source_name: IMF/World Bank FSAP — Montenegro Financial Sector Assessment Program technical notes
candidates.why_relevant: FSAP technical notes (banking supervision, stress testing, crisis management/resolution, AML) generate multi-year recommendation lists that Montenegrin authorities then implement; subsequent Article IVs explicitly track FSAP-recommendation implementation, making the FSAP the anchor document for a dated reform backlog.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off backfill of all Montenegro FSAP notes; then watch for a new FSAP cycle announcement in Article IV press releases.
queries_used: IMF World Bank Montenegro financial sector assessment recommendations

candidates.source_name: European Commission — Montenegro Enlargement Report (SWD), Chapters 4, 9, 24, 32
candidates.why_relevant: The annual Country Report is the most granular external audit of Montenegro's financial-services acquis alignment (Ch.9 Financial services, Ch.4 Free movement of capital incl. AML, Ch.32 Financial control). It states, chapter by chapter, what remains to be transposed — effectively an English-language forward regulatory calendar for banks and PSPs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual fetch of the Montenegro Report PDF (autumn enlargement package) + diff against prior year to isolate new obligations; also poll the news feed for interim benchmarks/IBAR decisions.
queries_used: European Commission Montenegro Report chapter 4 9 financial services enlargement package

candidates.source_name: European Commission — Montenegro accession financial package / negotiating framework communications
candidates.why_relevant: The June 2026 financial package communication for Montenegro's accession negotiations sets the fiscal and chapter-closing timetable that conditions when financial-services acquis chapters must be provisionally closed — an upstream driver of regulatory deadlines.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Event-driven fetch triggered by the enlargement newsroom RSS.
queries_used: European Commission Montenegro Report chapter 4 9 financial services enlargement package

candidates.source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — MoU with the Central Bank of Montenegro / international cooperation register
candidates.why_relevant: The 2018 ECB(SSM)–CBCG Memorandum of Understanding governs supervisory information exchange for EU banking-group subsidiaries in Montenegro (the market is dominated by EU-parent banks). New or amended MoUs signal changes in consolidated supervision and in how EU-level supervisory expectations reach Montenegrin subsidiaries.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency (quarterly) crawl of the MoU register page, diff the list of counterparties/documents.
queries_used: EBA Montenegro supervisory cooperation memorandum third country central bank

candidates.source_name: EBA — third-country equivalence, professional-secrecy assessments and SEE Memorandum of Cooperation
candidates.why_relevant: EBA equivalence guidelines determine whether the CBCG's confidentiality regime is treated as EU-equivalent (Montenegro assessed positively), which gates supervisory-college participation and cross-border data flows. The 2015 Vienna-Initiative SEE Memorandum of Cooperation, to which Montenegro is a signatory, is the operating framework.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Watch the EBA press-release feed filtered for 'equivalence', 'South Eastern', 'Montenegro'; archive the MoC PDF.
queries_used: EBA Montenegro supervisory cooperation memorandum third country central bank

candidates.source_name: European Payments Council — SEPA geographical scope, scheme country list and adherence calendar
candidates.why_relevant: The EPC sets the binding operational dates for Montenegrin PSP adherence to SCT, SCT Inst and SDD (adherence enabled from April 2025; Operational Readiness Date 5 Oct 2025). The versioned 'EPC List of SEPA Scheme Countries' (v7.0 May 2025, v8.0 Dec 2025) is a dated, structured artefact for tracking Montenegrin PSP scheme participation.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track the versioned EPC409-09 country-list PDF and the EPC Register of Participants; diff Montenegrin PSP entries per scheme release cycle (Nov and May).
queries_used: European Payments Council SEPA scheme Montenegro participation geographical scope

candidates.source_name: BIS — CPMI payment/FMI statistics portal and country payment-system information (Red Book)
candidates.why_relevant: BIS/CPMI provides the methodological standard (d168) and comparative Red Book payment statistics against which Montenegrin RTGS/DNS data published by the CBCG can be benchmarked. Montenegro is not a CPMI member so it is not in the Red Book series itself — value is methodological and comparative rather than country-specific.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Pull SDMX/CSV comparative tables from data.bis.org annually as a benchmarking baseline; use d168 as the schema for normalising CBCG payment statistics.
queries_used: BIS CPMI Montenegro payment systems red book Central Bank of Montenegro BIS statistics

candidates.source_name: World Bank — Western Balkans Regular Economic Report (financial-sector chapter)
candidates.why_relevant: Semi-annual (spring/autumn) report with a dedicated financial-sector section and a Montenegro country note; provides comparable cross-Western-Balkans framing of credit growth, NPLs, financial inclusion and regulatory reform progress in English.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Semi-annual PDF fetch (documents1.worldbank.org / openknowledge); extract the Montenegro country note and the financial-sector special topic.
queries_used: World Bank Montenegro financial sector Western Balkans Regular Economic Report

candidates.source_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports — Montenegro corpus
candidates.why_relevant: Full-text searchable archive of World Bank analytical work on Montenegro (including Montenegrin-language editions, e.g. the 'Crna Gora: Priprema za prosperitet' report), development policy operations with financial-sector prior actions, and FSAP-linked technical assistance. Best single pointer for discovering less-visible assessments.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Repository API/OAI-PMH query filtered on country=Montenegro and topic=Finance and Financial Sector Development; monthly incremental harvest.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from World Bank search results (incl. a Montenegrin-language hit)
queries_used: MMF izvještaj Crna Gora bankarski sektor preporuke Član IV
World Bank Montenegro financial sector

candidates.source_name: EBRD — Transition Report country assessment: Montenegro
candidates.why_relevant: The annual Transition Report Montenegro assessment flags concrete regulatory pressure points — e.g. political pressure on the central bank over lending-rate caps, AML/CFT framework gaps, and real-estate inflow risks — often earlier and more bluntly than domestic sources. EBRD country strategies also set financial-sector reform conditionality.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual fetch of the Transition Report Montenegro country-assessment PDF plus event-driven capture of country-strategy documents and press releases.
queries_used: EBRD Montenegro financial sector diagnostic transition report banking

candidates.source_name: EIB / Vienna Initiative — CESEE Bank Lending Survey
candidates.why_relevant: Semi-annual survey of ~15 international banking groups and ~85 local subsidiaries covering Montenegro; captures parent-bank strategy toward the Montenegrin market, credit supply/demand conditions and NPL trends. Indirect for regulation, but a strong leading indicator of where supervisory attention will land.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Semi-annual PDF + accompanying dataset download; extract Montenegro-specific panels where disaggregated.
queries_used: Vienna Initiative CESEE bank lending survey Montenegro

candidates.source_name: S&P Global Ratings — Montenegro sovereign rating actions and research updates
candidates.why_relevant: Sovereign rating rationales contain a structured banking-sector section (BICRA-style commentary, credit growth, external position, EU-parent bank funding). Rating actions are dated, scheduled (published sovereign review calendar) and freely readable in the EU regulatory-disclosure section without subscription.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the EU regulatory-disclosure article feed on the published sovereign review calendar dates; store metadata and short quotes only (content is copyrighted).
queries_used: Montenegro country risk rating banking sector regulatory outlook

candidates.source_name: Moody's Ratings — Montenegro sovereign credit opinion and global banking outlooks
candidates.why_relevant: Moody's affirmed Montenegro at Ba3 and moved the outlook to positive (reported March 2026) explicitly citing EU-accession progress; its credit opinions discuss banking-system health and contingent liabilities. Moody's also owns the Basel-AML-Index-adjacent KYC analytics used in country-risk screening.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Capture free press-release headlines and dates; corroborate via secondary trade press (SeeNews, MINA) where the full opinion is paywalled. Do not redistribute full text.
queries_used: Moody's Montenegro sovereign rating banking sector outlook 2026
candidates.observed_blocker: Full Moody's credit opinions require a subscription/registration; only press releases and outlook summaries are openly readable.

candidates.source_name: Basel Institute on Governance — Basel AML Index (public ranking edition)
candidates.why_relevant: Composite ML/TF country risk score built from ~17 public sources including FATF/MONEYVAL evaluation data; gives a comparable annual Montenegro risk trajectory that correspondent banks and compliance teams actually use. Useful as an aggregator that translates the Montenegrin AML framework into a comparable number.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual capture of the public ranking edition PDF and the Montenegro row from index.baselgovernance.org; store score time-series only.
queries_used: Basel AML Index Montenegro country risk score
candidates.observed_blocker: Public ranking is free; the expert edition with full sub-indicator data is licensed.

candidates.source_name: US State Department — INCSR Volume II (Money Laundering), Montenegro country chapter
candidates.why_relevant: Annual, dated, third-country assessment of Montenegro's AML regime naming specific structural weaknesses (financial-investigation capacity, inter-agency cooperation, judicial independence, laundering via construction/real estate and games of chance). Frequently more candid than EU/CoE texts and used by correspondent banks in de-risking decisions.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF fetch (usually released Feb-Mar) and extraction of the Montenegro section; archive historical volumes from the 2009-2017 and 2021-2025 archived state.gov subdomains.
queries_used: US State Department INCSR Montenegro money laundering

candidates.source_name: GRECO (Council of Europe) — Montenegro evaluation and compliance reports
candidates.why_relevant: GRECO compliance reports set dated recommendation-implementation deadlines on integrity, beneficial ownership and law-enforcement governance that overlap with AML/CFT obligations on financial institutions. Reports are published in both English and Montenegrin on rm.coe.int, making it a rare bilingual assessor source.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the country evaluations page after each GRECO plenary; harvest both the EN and the Montenegrin-language rm.coe.int PDFs.
queries_used: GRECO evaluation report Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: Government of Montenegro (gov.me) — official Montenegrin-language reporting on MONEYVAL/IMF outcomes
candidates.why_relevant: The Montenegrin authorities' own local-language read-out of external assessments is the fastest indicator of which assessor recommendations the government intends to act on and by when. It names the specific legal instruments amended (Zakon o sprječavanju pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma, pravilnici) and the plenary dates — a bridge between the assessor cell and domestic implementation.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-filtered crawl of gov.me news (MONEYVAL, MMF, FATF, preporuke) plus the wapi.gov.me document download endpoints for attached reports.
queries_used: MONEYVAL izvještaj Crna Gora preporuke sprječavanje pranja novca
local_language_terms_used: sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma

candidates.source_name: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) — AML/CFT supervision page and international-cooperation section
candidates.why_relevant: Although CBCG is a domestic regulator (other cells' primary territory), for THIS cell it is the counterparty page where assessor recommendations surface as supervisory practice, and where MoUs with ECB/EBA and SEPA milestones are confirmed in Montenegrin. Useful for verifying that an assessor recommendation has been operationalised.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Targeted crawl of the AML supervision and press-release sections in both /me and /en locales; use as verification layer for assessor-driven changes.
queries_used: MONEYVAL izvještaj Crna Gora preporuke sprječavanje pranja novca
local_language_terms_used: nadzor u oblasti sprečavanja pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma

candidates.source_name: Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma (Montenegro FIU) — national reporting to assessors
candidates.why_relevant: The Montenegrin FIU is the national counterpart that drafts the country's MONEYVAL follow-up submissions and national risk assessments; its documents are the domestic mirror of the assessor cycle and are published in Montenegrin via gov.me/wapi.gov.me download endpoints.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the FIU's gov.me organisational subsite for documents/reports; the exact subsite slug should be confirmed by a live pass.
queries_used: MONEYVAL izvještaj Crna Gora preporuke sprječavanje pranja novca
candidates.observed_blocker: The organisational subsite URL is inferred from the gov.me URL pattern and was not opened; treat as unverified.

candidates.source_name: eucrim (Max Planck / EU criminal-law journal) — MONEYVAL & GRECO Montenegro report digests
candidates.why_relevant: Concise, reliably dated English digests of each new MONEYVAL/GRECO Montenegro report with direct links to the primary PDFs. An efficient low-volume tripwire for detecting that a new assessor report exists before building the full crawl.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/news-feed subscription filtered on 'Montenegro', 'MONEYVAL', 'GRECO'; follow through to primary sources rather than storing the digest text.
queries_used: MONEYVAL Montenegro follow-up report AML compliance

candidates.source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa (RFE/RL Balkan Service) — local-language coverage of assessor processes
candidates.why_relevant: Investigative local-language reporting on the politics of external assessment — e.g. coverage of Montenegro lobbying to avoid enhanced AML monitoring. Captures the pre-decision phase (lobbying, negotiation, contested findings) that official assessor documents never record.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword feed monitoring (pranje novca, MONEYVAL, siva lista, FATF) with metadata + short-quote storage only.
queries_used: MONEYVAL izvještaj Crna Gora preporuke sprječavanje pranja novca

candidates.source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin specialist banking/finance trade portal
candidates.why_relevant: Local-language trade portal that reports assessor findings (IMF stress-test results, MONEYVAL ratings, EBRD warnings) in banking-industry framing and carries reaction from Montenegrin banks and the banking association — the domestic interpretation layer on top of the assessor documents.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/site crawl with keyword filter (MMF, MONEYVAL, CBCG, supervizija, preporuke); store links and short excerpts.
queries_used: MMF izvještaj Crna Gora bankarski sektor preporuke Član IV

negative_findings.description: Montenegro is not a CPMI member jurisdiction, so BIS Red Book payment and FMI statistics do not contain a Montenegro series. Searches surfaced only the CPMI methodology (d168), the BIS data portal and the CBCG's own RTGS/DNS statistics.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Montenegro rows found in the BIS CPMI Red Book dataset; BIS value for this cell is methodological/comparative only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Payment-system benchmarking for Montenegro must be built from CBCG-published RTGS/DNS data normalised to the CPMI schema, not pulled from BIS directly.

negative_findings.description: No evidence was found of an EBA or ECB opinion, guideline or assessment addressed specifically to Montenegro beyond the SEE Memorandum of Cooperation (2015), the ECB-CBCG MoU (2018) and the professional-secrecy equivalence assessment.
negative_findings.result_summary: EBA/ECB engagement with Montenegro appears to be framework-level (MoU, equivalence) rather than country-opinion-level.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell rationale's expectation of 'EBA/ECB opinions' on Montenegro is only partially met; monitoring effort should be weighted toward MONEYVAL, IMF and the EC enlargement report instead.

negative_findings.description: No established Montenegrin-language terminology was found for BIS/CPMI concepts (Red Book, financial market infrastructures) or for credit-rating methodology terms; domestic coverage uses English terms or loose paraphrase.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language search for BIS/CPMI and rating-agency methodology in Montenegrin returned no usable native glossary.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring for those sub-topics must rely on the English acronyms (BIS, CPMI, Moody's, S&P, Fitch, Ba3) embedded in Montenegrin-language text rather than on translated terms.

negative_findings.description: Full rating reports from Moody's, and the expert edition of the Basel AML Index, are behind subscription or licensing.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only press releases, outlook summaries and the free public ranking are openly accessible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A rating-driven early-warning feed for Montenegro cannot be built from primary CRA text alone; it must lean on free regulatory-disclosure pages (S&P) plus secondary trade-press relay (SeeNews, MINA, bankar.me).

negative_findings.description: Several canonical landing-page URLs in this slice (MONEYVAL Montenegro jurisdiction page, IMF country page, EBRD Montenegro country page, Moody's Montenegro issuer page, Montenegro FIU subsite) were constructed from the publishers' standard URL patterns and from search-result context rather than opened directly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Deep-link example_urls came from search results and are high confidence; the top-level landing URLs are pattern-inferred and should be treated as unverified pending the deterministic liveness pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a false 'verified' claim; the liveness pass should prioritise these landing pages, and a 403/timeout on coe.int or imf.org should be read as bot defence, not as a dead source.

coverage_gaps.description: Fitch Ratings coverage of Montenegro was not confirmed in this pass; only Moody's (Ba3, positive) and S&P were evidenced. Whether Fitch maintains a Montenegro sovereign rating is unresolved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a targeted pass on fitchratings.com for a Montenegro sovereign entity page and on the ESMA CRA register / countryeconomy.com aggregator to establish which agencies actually rate Montenegro and on what calendar.

coverage_gaps.description: The IMF/World Bank FSAP evidence found is dated (2015-2016 cycle plus 2019 report). Whether a newer Montenegro FSAP has been scheduled or delivered was not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search the IMF FSAP page and recent Article IV staff reports for an FSAP update announcement; if none, record that FSAP recommendations are tracked only indirectly via annual Article IV follow-up language.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language (sr/Montenegrin) discovery in this cell was productive for MONEYVAL/AML and IMF terms but shallow for supervisory-cooperation, SEPA/payment-scheme and EU-acquis-chapter terminology.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend local-language querying with terms such as 'jedinstveno područje plaćanja u eurima', 'sporazum o saradnji u superviziji', 'poglavlje 9 finansijske usluge', 'pregovaračko poglavlje', 'mjerila za zatvaranje poglavlja'.

coverage_gaps.description: No structured deadline/commitment tracker was identified. Assessor deadlines are currently scattered across MONEYVAL follow-up cycles, EC annual reports and IMF Article IV commitments with no single machine-readable calendar.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an internal derived calendar entity keyed on (assessor, report_date, next_report_due, recommendation_id) populated from the MONEYVAL FUR annex, the EC report chapter tables and the IMF staff-report policy matrix.

coverage_gaps.description: Council of Europe / EU joint technical-assistance projects in Montenegro (e.g. the AML capacity-building programmes referenced by EEAS and the Rule of Law Platform) were noted but not mapped as sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map coe.int Horizontal Facility and rolplatform.org Montenegro project pages, which publish assessor-aligned progress reporting and workshop outputs on a project timetable.

brief: Montenegro's external-assessor landscape is unusually dense and well-documented in English, which makes this cell the most efficient route into the country's regulatory calendar. Four sources dominate: MONEYVAL/FATF (5th-round MER 2023 plus enhanced follow-up adopted at the December 2025 plenary, with a one-year report-back obligation), the IMF Article IV cycle (2025 consultation concluded 18 November 2025, flagging credit growth, cash loans, real-estate exposure and AML enforcement), the European Commission's annual enlargement Country Report (the granular Chapter 4/9/24/32 acquis audit), and the European Payments Council, which set hard operational dates for Montenegrin PSP entry into SEPA (adherence from April 2025, Operational Readiness Date 5 October 2025). Secondary layers — EBRD Transition Report, World Bank Western Balkans REB, US INCSR, GRECO, Basel AML Index and the rating agencies — add candour and comparability but are weaker on dated commitments, and BIS/CPMI carries no Montenegro series since the country is not a CPMI member. Local-language sources (gov.me read-outs, CBCG, bankar.me, Slobodna Evropa) matter here less as primary assessment and more as the fastest signal of which assessor recommendations the authorities intend to implement, and when.
